events.title: Pope Martin I is arrested for opposing Monothelitism
events.description: Pope Martin I, an opponent of Monothelitism, was arrested in the Lateran in Rome with Maximus the Confessor on the orders of Emperor Constans II and taken to Constantinople. He was later banished to Cherson, where he died.

events.title: Caliph Uthman is assassinated in Medina
events.description: Rebels besieging the house of Uthman ibn Affan, the third Rashidun caliph, who had refused their demand for a new caliph, set it on fire, broke in and killed him. His murder triggered the First Fitna, a civil war.

events.title: Empress Matilda marries Geoffrey of Anjou at Le Mans
events.description: Matilda, widow of Emperor Henry V and the nominated heir of Henry I of England, married Geoffrey, the son of Fulk of Anjou, at Le Mans; she was 25 and he was 13. The marriage proved difficult, and she soon left him for Normandy.

events.title: Vlad the Impaler attacks the Ottoman camp by night
events.description: Vlad III of Wallachia led a night raid on Sultan Mehmed II's camp near Târgovişte, failing to kill the sultan. His reputation for cruelty later fed the legend behind Bram Stoker's Dracula.

events.title: Francis Drake claims Nova Albion for Elizabeth I
events.description: During his circumnavigation, Drake landed on the coast of what is now northern California and claimed it for England as Nova Albion. England made no attempt to settle it.

events.title: Mumtaz Mahal dies in childbirth at Burhanpur
events.description: Mumtaz Mahal, chief consort of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, died in Burhanpur giving birth to her 14th child while accompanying him on a campaign in the Deccan. Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in Agra to house her tomb.

events.title: British take Breed's Hill at heavy cost in the Battle of Bunker Hill
events.description: After two failed assaults, British troops drove colonial militia from the heights near Boston. They suffered more than 1,000 casualties, proving the Americans could stand against regulars.
events.html: After two failed assaults, British troops drove colonial militia from the heights near Boston. They suffered more than 1,000 casualties, proving the Americans could stand against regulars.

events.title: Iceland becomes a republic
events.description: At Þingvellir, the site of its ancient assembly, Iceland ended its union with the Danish crown and proclaimed a republic. Denmark was then under German occupation.

events.title: Five men are arrested in the Watergate building
events.description: Burglars linked to President Nixon's re-election committee were caught inside the Democratic National Committee offices in Washington. The cover-up led to Nixon's resignation in 1974.

events.title: O. J. Simpson leads police on a televised chase
events.description: About 95 million viewers watched police follow a white Ford Bronco carrying the former football star along Los Angeles freeways. Simpson was later acquitted of murdering his ex-wife and her friend.

song: Goliards, the Latin poets of the Carmina Burana
A Latin poem from about 800 years ago about Fortune, who spins a wheel that lifts people up and throws them down.
